predicted_signals.evidence: Family member describing deceased: 'Noa was a child of light, of love, of joy, of giving. Always saw the weak, always sought to contribute without expecting anything in return.' Family reopened cafe in her memory as positive commemoration and continued giving.
Family reopened cafe 'Chatzer shel Noni' after year of mourning, renovated space with father and deceased's father, established agricultural shop with Israeli products only
Council head: 'We won every battle against Hezbollah, but it does not translate to a decision that ends this story once and for all. That is what saddens me. We fell into the trap in a sense.'
Council head requests residents remain in homes and minimize movement due to ongoing security risks from rocket fire
Senior officer at base humiliated newly discharged female soldiers with derogatory and discriminatory remarks, brought them to show trial for wearing jeans and jacket
Settlement patrol officer immediately responded to infiltration alert at 6:07, jumped to gate area, confronted armed attacker with knife, neutralized threat within minutes
Settlement defense systems detected infiltration, alert activated, patrol officer neutralized armed knife-wielding attacker, no casualties, IDF conducted area sweeps
Kiryat Shmona municipality announced general strike in education and city services (except emergency), organized bus convoy for protest actions across country
Kiryat Shmona municipality announced general strike in education and city services (except emergency), organized bus convoy for protest actions
Zavik Gelidai (78) was teaching online when a drone battery from Lebanon fell in his garden. He went outside and approached the debris to inspect it, discovering explosive material nearby.
Zavik Gelidai: 'To my joy, nothing happened except a hole in the trampoline.' He expressed relief that the drone debris caused minimal damage despite containing explosive material.
Magen David Adom established an emergency primary response clinic inside a shelter in Kibbutz Misgav Am

MDA undertook establishment of clinic with assistance of MDA Chief Paramedic Dr. Shafir Botner and Head of Immediate Response Department Yossi Halabi; residents received training and refreshers in first aid
MDA paramedic Igor Krasni: 'This clinic is going to change the situation on the ground for us'
Kibbutz secretary Erez Bergman: 'We appreciate tremendously the establishment of this clinic. We are right on the border and have basic needs that must be met'

During final barrages before ceasefire took effect, sirens sounded across Nahariya, Evron, Liman, Shlomi and Gesher HaZiv. In Nahariya one person was moderately wounded and vehicles caught fire. In Karmiel area, a man in his mid-20s and 17-year-old girl were seriously wounded.
An alert sounded in Natufa in Western Galilee about 2 hours after ceasefire took effect, but Home Front Command clarified it was a false alarm with no actual rocket fire from Lebanon.

During final barrages before ceasefire, 8 people were wounded in northern Israel: 2 seriously (a 25-year-old motorcyclist with leg and head injuries, a 17-year-old girl with shrapnel leg injury), 1 moderately (40-year-old man with facial injury), and 5 trauma casualties.

Mrom HaGalil Regional Council head Amit Sofer stated: 'It is not reasonable that Trump will tie the Lebanese arena to the Iranian arena... he is condemning the residents of the north to years of ongoing threat.' He expressed preference for continued military operations over a ceasefire that leaves Hezbollah intact.
In southern village of Jibsheet, displaced residents returned to find flattened apartment blocks, streets littered with concrete chunks, twisted aluminum shutters and dangling electrical wires.

23-year-old Zainab Fahas said: 'I feel free being back. But look, they destroyed everything: the square, the houses, the shops, everything.' Ali Hamza said: 'People are scared to come and live, and it is impossible to live in these circumstances, and with these smells. A full return is difficult now, despite the hardship of displacement.'

Bedouin residents of Wadi al-Naam living adjacent to the Naot Hovav petrochemical industrial zone have no way to defend themselves against missile attacks or dangerous chemical leaks from factories. High-voltage lines and underground gas pipelines run through the area with minimal safety infrastructure.

Despite IDF warnings not to return south of the Litani River until further notice, Lebanese residents began driving back toward their homes in southern Lebanon when the ceasefire took effect, creating traffic jams on roads between Beirut and Sidon.
Lebanese residents celebrated the ceasefire by taking to streets in Beirut and driving convoys toward southern Lebanon despite warnings from both IDF and Lebanese Army not to return to the area.

Displaced residents from southern Lebanon began driving back toward their homes despite IDF warnings not to move south of the Litani River until further notice, creating traffic congestion on roads between Beirut and Sidon.
Head of Akko municipality Ohad Shagiv directed the Education Department to prepare for full reopening of schools starting Sunday, pending Home Front Command approval and assessment of the situation.
Akko municipality announced full reopening of all educational institutions starting Sunday, following a situation assessment by the Home Front Command in the Western Galilee district.
Ramat Hasharon beach parking lots filled to capacity due to surge in visitors following ceasefire, with municipality requesting public to use public transportation or nearby parking instead.

Lebanese civilians broke through earthen barriers placed on the Al-Qasmiya Bridge over the Litani River and crossed south despite IDF warnings, using the central bridge that was not destroyed by Israel.

Residents of Kiryat Shmona expressed frustration with the ceasefire announcement. Liraz Chernayev said: 'I have a strong sense of déjà vu. Again they are stopping the fighting at its peak. In 2024 they told us Hezbollah was weakened and had no commanders, but after a year and a half rockets and drones flew at us again.' Shlomo Suysa said: 'A new prime minister is imposed on us in the name of Trump—and on northern residents a death sentence is imposed. I feel deceived and frustrated.' Moshe Kakon said: 'This is a cynical move of surrender to Iranian demands.'

Ministry of Defense: 170 fallen soldiers added to count since last Memorial Day; 54 disabled IDF members recognized as fallen this year. Total fallen since 1860: 25,644. Since October 7, 2023: 7,165 new bereaved family members added.
59,583 bereaved family members now live in Israel: 8,420 bereaved parents, 4,872 widows, 14,430 children of fallen soldiers, 31,814 siblings, 12 fiancées, 35 guardians.

KKL-JNF announces NIS 30 million budget to give around 15,000 northern residents living up to 9 kilometers from the border five days in hotels with half board, free transportation and activities; also budgeted NIS 800,000 to take school pupils away from border area to quieter classrooms.
KKL launched first respite program in late March, taking 6,000 people living within 2 kilometers of Lebanese border for two-night hotel rest.

National Parents' Leadership stated that the matriculation easement framework 'does not provide a real answer to the central need of students—reducing burden and pressure as promised.' Oren Ozen, chair of the national parents' leadership, said: 'These are only point measures that do not reduce the burden in practice and do not change the daily reality in schools.'

Education Minister Yoav Kish expanded matriculation relief measures: students can choose one humanities subject for internal exam instead of external; northern students receive additional accommodations including adapted math questions and grade bonuses.

Dozens of Palestinian children unable to go to school in West Bank village of Umm al-Khair because barbed wire erected by Jewish settlers from nearby Carmel settlement blocked their usual safe path through a valley.

Khalil Hathaleen, head of Umm al-Khair village council, reported Israeli soldiers fired teargas, causing several children to experience breathing difficulties; residents described children's symptoms as if they were suffocating.
Israel Memorial Day 2026: 170 soldiers killed, 79 victims of terror since last year

Amit Sofer, head of Mrom HaGalil regional council, said: 'Residents of the front line want real security, not industrial quiet. Even though sleeping several nights in a row is very tempting, we are asking the Israeli government to continue striking Hezbollah until its disarmament.'
5-year-old child killed by vehicle impact on Hazon Ish Street in Beit Shemesh. Transported in critical condition to Shaare Zedek Hospital where death was pronounced after resuscitation efforts.
'Step by Step' program operates under Belev Echad, helping 18 wounded soldiers rebuild routine and purpose through intensive physical training, supporting recovery from injury and PTSD
Wounded soldiers in program are coping with ongoing symptoms of Post-traumatic stress disorder; many arrive with no routine, no sleep, no physical baseline
A resident described weeks of sleep punctuated by sirens, working from home while caring for children, and then being told to return to the office immediately.

Behind the veneer of Israel's famed resilience, darker feelings are simmering. Parents express pessimism: 'Can we all just get a paid spa day while our kids are in school before we go back to our bomb shelters?' and 'I'm trying to do as much as I can now before the war starts up again.'
Children were sent back to school just hours after ceasefire began, after weeks of canceled classes and scattershot online learning. Cafes and beaches filled once again with Israelis.
Israelis are relieved they no longer have to plan their lives around proximity to bomb shelters, and restrictions on gatherings have been lifted. Many are embracing a return to normalcy.

Ministry of Education announced a framework of easements in matriculation exams divided by three regions: the front line, the Gulf area and southern Golan, and the rest of the country, including options for internal exams instead of external exams in humanities subjects.
Shrapnel from Hezbollah rocket strike severely wounded a 25-year-old man in Carmiel; three others treated for stress symptoms
Three people treated for stress symptoms following Hezbollah rocket barrage

Kfar Vardim council informed residents: 'Hezbollah may increase fire in the coming hours. It is recommended to stay near protected spaces and be attentive to Home Front Command instructions. All activities will be stopped.' Maaleh Yosef reported: 'Despite no formal order from Northern Command, there is increased likelihood of rocket fire in the coming hours.'

Tens of thousands of IDF wounded are undergoing complex rehabilitation. 'Beit HaLohem' provides emotional support; 'For Success' program offers comprehensive rehabilitation including physiotherapy, climbing training, and employment pathway 'Recalculating Route' with dedicated employment department.

Bereaved parent Goren: 'It is a very respectful and human place. There are many fallen soldiers from the war there, and my parents are there as well. It allows people to connect to the pain of what has happened here over the past three years.'

Less than two hours before the ceasefire took effect at midnight, Hezbollah fired barrages at northern settlements. Medical services reported a man and a girl severely wounded in Carmiel (ages 25 and 17). In Nahariya, a man around 40 was moderately wounded by shrapnel. Two vehicles caught fire in the city. Five people were treated for shock and evacuated to Nahariya hospital.

Hotel Association launched initiative to honor reserve personnel for Independence Day 78: second night at 50% discount or third night free for those who served 30+ days in 2026. Campaign runs through Saturday; stays April 19-24.
30 public and educational facilities damaged in Arad missile strike, including city's cultural hall and community center
Many have recently been complaining about mental fog, difficulty concentrating, irritability, or a decline in mood after almost three years of living in the shadow of endless wars on various fronts.
Ari Spitz, severely wounded IDF soldier: 'Let's try to find as many people as possible who promote togetherness and emphasize the importance of listening to one another, and less division.'

Ari Spitz: 'Today I'm a law student. Rehabilitation is a lifelong process, and I still have a few surgeries ahead of me, and I'm combining everything.' Hopes Israel will achieve 'clear victory in what he described as a just war on all fronts.'

'Amit's Friends Café' operates year-round as a community initiative connecting people around the memory of Amit, who fell in combat in Rafah in August 2024. The café was founded by his family and local community with the desire to continue the simple moments Amit loved most—sitting with friends, talking, laughing and being together.
Israeli Ministry of Defense: 25,644 Israeli service members killed in action from 1860 to present; 170 fallen soldiers added since last Memorial Day
59,583 bereaved family members living in Israel: 8,420 bereaved parents, 4,872 widows/widowers, 14,430 orphans; 7,165 became bereaved since October 2023

Rabbi Doron Peretz, father of Daniel, said: 'Daniel was buried twice. At first we buried his shirt with blood. It was the only grave without a body. Now when I come there, he is there. His body was buried. On one hand, thank God he is not a hostage anymore, but now it is the reality of bereavement. Even though this is the third Memorial Day, it is the first one where Daniel is really there.' Shay, father of Tomer, described: 'For us, the circle did not close when we buried Tomer. Until they returned his brothers we did not mourn as we wanted. Now that everyone is buried, this is the hardest year. It is a seal that drags the loss. It did not become easier, it became harder.'

Barrage of fire on northern Israel: 8 casualties transported to Galilee Medical Center in Nahariya, including 2 severe (25-year-old motorcyclist with leg and head injury; 17-year-old girl with shrapnel leg injury), 1 moderate, 5 anxiety casualties.

MDA paramedic Maor Barko: 'We found a 25-year-old man on the floor, disoriented, suffering severe injuries to his body after being wounded by shrapnel from interception. We provided life-saving medical care and transported him to hospital in critical condition.'
A man in his mid-20s was seriously wounded near Karmiel as a result of Hezbollah strike; several people treated for acute anxiety
Several people suffering from acute anxiety following Hezbollah barrage

Emek Medical Center built and trained significant protected infrastructure in the last three years, including underground protected complexes housing ~300 hospital beds and 10 operating rooms, allowing the hospital to function flexibly and efficiently even under fire and continue providing full medical services to over one million residents.

Sderot launches pilot program to improve housing conditions by reducing 'energy poverty' — 20-30% of households pay for energy loss due to poor insulation. Professional teams conduct energy audits and develop tailored action plans.
Poll findings: 'despair and pessimism as dominant sentiments, alongside high levels of fatigue and clear expectation that conflict is far from over'

Minister Miri Regev stated: 'Our goal is to broadcast the ceremony live for the glory of the state. But we are also preparing for a filmed ceremony in case the ceasefire does not hold and we have other security events.' The state is pre-recording the torch-lighting ceremony as a contingency.

Memorial Day ceremonies will be held in accordance with Home Front Command wartime restrictions; state ceremonies will be filmed in advance and broadcast on TV and digital platforms if in-person events cannot take place.
Home Front Command wartime restrictions limit gatherings to 5,000 attendees in some areas of the north, West Bank, Jerusalem and the south; 1,000 people in central Israel and other areas.

Initiative 'Victory in the Living Room' organized by bereaved families and soldiers will host hundreds of fighters and bereaved families in Israeli homes on Memorial Day eve for remembrance and valor meetings sharing stories of battles and Israeli spirit.
האירוע המסורתי של יום העצמאות בוטל בשל המצב הביטחוני והנחיות פיקוד העורף

Ziv Medical Center in Safed gradually returning hospital departments and outpatient clinics to original above-ground locations after months of operating from underground fortified complexes; coordinated with security authorities and Health Ministry
Ziv Medical Center director Professor Salman Zarqa stated: 'We work with responsibility and caution, maintaining full readiness to return to fortification at any moment if necessary'

Research on Gaza envelope residents: 71% reported deterioration in general health; 40% taking or considering medication to cope; 58% showing hypervigilance; suffering from sleep disorders, chronic fatigue, and abdominal pain from chronic stress.
מגישת ערוץ 14 נוי בר: 'ילדתי תחת טילים, ראיתי כוכבים מהכאב'
בעת הלידה התרחשה מתקפת טילים; הובלה לחדר לידה ממוגן בשל מתקפה שהתרחשה באותן דקות
13-year-old student in Be'er Ya'akov targeted by coordinated cyberbullying campaign with fake obituary notice and TikTok page designed to intensify social boycott

Business owner in Galilee: 'There's no work, no income, but expenses continue as usual. Rent, employees, suppliers. It's an impossible situation... Couriers don't enter the area. There are orders that haven't been collected in weeks. Drivers are in reserves, there's no continuity of work—everything is broken.'

Business owner describes shelter inadequacy: 'There's not enough protection. In one alert dozens of people are crammed into one shelter, and there's no room for everyone. People are afraid to come, and workers are afraid to work in such conditions.'

Village of Sha-Nur in northern Samaria reconnected to national electricity grid; two electricity company workers who disconnected power 20 years ago performed the reconnection, symbolizing restoration of services
Armed civilian at Doron Valley Farm prevented stabbing attack by drawing personal firearm and shooting terrorist who attempted to stab Israeli civilians

Authorities and regional councils in the northern border area issued immediate warnings to residents to stay close to protected spaces due to concrete indications of imminent missile fire from Lebanon
Hezbollah fired dozens of rockets, sending tens of thousands of Israelis to bomb shelters
Hezbollah rocket barrage wounding one Israeli
Reauvén Barsheshet describes injury from service: 'The pain from the injury during service was also psychological.' He reports loss of sensation, inability to move his hand, and had to stop serving.
Residents and shoppers in Netivot experienced panic when tens of thousands of bees invaded the commercial center; people screamed and fled to enclosed spaces
Business owners in the commercial center closed shop doors and windows in response to the bee swarm
גבר בן 61 נפצע באורח קל מרסיסים בגפיים בטמרה בעקבות מטח שיגורי רקטות מלבנון
Civil air traffic largely curtailed following October 7 attack; many foreign carriers repeatedly suspended or canceled Tel Aviv routes
State Comptroller found no procedure in place to prioritize return of Israeli passengers abroad during war; soldiers and reservists struggled with air travel options and bore high financial burdens

Bank of Israel extended the enrollment window for war-affected households and businesses support framework by one additional month, allowing payment deferrals, mortgage extensions, and increased credit lines.
ראשי רשויות בצפון פרסמו הודעות לתושביהן כי ישנה התראה על מטחי ירי של חיזבאללה בטווח הזמן הקרוב
עמית סופר, ראש המועצה האזורית מרום הגליל: 'תושבי קו העימות רוצים ביטחון אמיתי ולא שקט תעשייתי... אנחנו מבקשים שממשלת ישראל תמשיך להכות בחיזבאללה עד לפירוקו מנשקו'

Yehali Ifirgan, 16-year-old student in Shlomi near Lebanon border: 'We're not prepared for the exam at all. If we were living in Ramat HaSharon or Tel Aviv and Hezbollah was shooting there, it would look completely different.'
שא-נור חוברה מחדש לרשת החשמל; עובדי חברת החשמל שהוריד את השאלטר בעת הגירוש הדליקו אותו מחדש
Nature and Parks Authority issued sharp warning to public planning to hike in Dead Sea, Negev, or Arava areas due to risk of flash floods on Friday; absolute prohibition on entering wadi channels

Of 11,000 Kiryat Shmona residents who requested a four-night respite break from shelters, more than half were left behind due to budget shortage. Only 4,600 places allocated; 8,500 residents from border communities went in first rotation; over 6,000 requests from the city were rejected.
המועצה האזורית גוש עציון חציתה רף של 30,000 תושבים; בשנה האחרונה הצטרפו 931 תושבים חדשים בקצב גידול של כ-3.6%

Police completed preparations for state cup semifinal match at Teddy Stadium in Jerusalem with 5,000 capacity limit per Home Front Command guidelines; deployed officers, security personnel, and traffic management

Independence Day central stages cancelled in most local authorities due to security situation and Home Front Command restrictions on mass gatherings, leaving thousands of artists, technicians, and production staff facing contract cancellations.

Local authorities agreed to book cancelled Independence Day artists for alternative events throughout the year (Jerusalem Day, summer events, holidays) to prevent economic harm to artists and production crews.

Ministry of Construction and Housing delayed opening of 'Apartment at Discount' lottery registration to advance emergency order allocating half of apartments to reserve duty soldiers, adding 1,139 apartments to soldier allocation in upcoming lottery

Six-year-old girl Shiba Badeer from Kafr Qasem died from brain hemorrhage; her family donated her organs, saving four children: 9-year-old girl received liver, 18-year-old girl received one kidney, 2.5-year-old boy received second kidney, 3.5-year-old toddler received heart.
State Comptroller report: no system in place to prioritize return of Israelis stranded abroad; soldiers and reservists forced to arrange own flights at significant personal cost
State Comptroller audit: no government body conducted comprehensive assessment of long-term economic impact from shortage of foreign and Palestinian workers following October 7
Two reserve soldiers' apartment in Netanya was burglarized while they were on duty; police closed the investigation without arrests. They reported theft of military equipment and 85,000 shekels.
IDF spokesman reports: one paratrooper severely wounded and four soldiers lightly wounded from rocket fire in southern Lebanon; evacuated to hospital

Abihai Stern, mayor of Kiryat Shmona: 'The current discussion is about formulating a national compensation framework for all business owners in Israel, and is not focused only on the north.' He was told he could not join via Zoom.
דובר צה״ל: יש לגלות עירנות, לנהוג באחריות ולהישמע להנחיות פיקוד העורף

Shira Shagev: 'It's moving on every level. We believed it would happen but not so fast... It's a great privilege to step here and drive on the roads again.' Adi Galbert: 'There are challenges but when you see the spirit is very strong the challenges shrink. There's something very natural here. The children are happy and joyful, there's something basic, special and powerful.'
Evacuees returning to Sha'ar Nur settlement; children playing and running in streets; families settling in temporary caravans; community resuming normal activities despite physical constraints

Home Front Command says wartime guidelines remain unchanged until Sunday night; educational activities permitted only inside bomb shelters in communities on Lebanon border; gatherings restricted to 5,000 in some areas of north, 1,000 in others
מיירטים של כיפת ברזל זוהו בטעות כטילים של חיזבאללה והפעילו אזעקות בגליל המערבי
המשטרה פנתה לציבור וביקשה מהתושבים להיות קשובים ולהשמע להנחיות, לא להגיע לאתרי נפילות טילים ולהימנע מנגיעה בשברי יירוט
Sirens have been sounding across the Galilee for the past half an hour, warning of rocket fire from Lebanon
Tzala Weiss (50), writing workshop facilitator: 'The war brought us business owners to the edge... I opened the business 11 years ago and never thought it would be harmed - it's my baby.'

Female soldier: 'Surrounded by enemies, facing my eyes Dura, El Fawwar and all the villages around - and meanwhile life in this small settlement continues... I stop for a moment and think who is guarding whom?'
Soldier protecting settlement residents; residents blessing soldier with 'Happy holiday' and 'Thank you'; note on wall saying 'Thank you for guarding us'
עצרת הנעילה המסורתית ליום הזיכרון לשואה ולגבורה בבית לוחמי הגטאות לא מתקיימת השנה פיזית אלא משודרת כמוקלטת בשל המצב הביטחוני
Nature reserve inspector reports that the vast majority of rescue cases involve yeshiva students; students ignoring professional field guidelines and safety instructions from reserve rangers
Ten soldiers wounded in fighting in southern Lebanon overnight, including three in serious condition, one moderate, six light wounds; all evacuated to hospitals

David Azulai: 'We had a relatively quiet night from both sides. There are those who say there will be escalation, in fact we see relative quiet since yesterday evening. This lights a red light for me. We want security here because that is the only thing I think can bring back the communities, young families, and we must have security. This has been lacking here for decades. We are tired of wars. We are two and a half years into war. We are tired. We need quiet.'

Chamber of Commerce Federation head Shahar Turgeman: 'The private sector is the generator that produces the current - without it there is no hope for the battery... The state must invest in the private sector because it's an investment that returns itself many times over.' Noted 65,000 businesses closed or went bankrupt in 2025, 61,000 in 2024 - negative balance.

Commander of Battalion 52, Lt. Col. 'A.', seriously wounded during operational activity in southern Lebanon; ten soldiers wounded in encounter—three seriously, one moderately, six lightly; all evacuated to hospital

Operation Saar HaAri placed Holocaust survivors in impossible security reality, but government response remained slow and cumbersome. Special committee discussions in March 2026 revealed no complete mapping of shelter infrastructure for elderly and Holocaust survivors. Older survivors lack accessible housing providing proper protection adapted to their needs.
רון גדסי, חברו של רס״ם ביאנקו: 'אייל היה הרוח החיה של הפלוגה שלנו, בחור ערכי שתמיד התנדב ראשון לכל משימה'

IDF reservist Eyal Uriel Bianco, age 30, killed when Humvee overturned in southern Lebanon. Three other reservists injured: one moderately, two lightly. Bianco was a firefighter driver in the 188 Barak Brigade, served hundreds of reserve days since start of war on February 28.
מיזם 'למלא את החלל' מאפשר לאנשים להקדיש מעשי חסד לזכר נופלים: התנדבות במד״א, נתינת צדקה, מעשים קהילתיים וחיתוך יומיומי
משפחות של נופלים מקבלות הודעה מיידית כאשר מישהו מקדיש מעשה טוב בזכרם, מה שמחייה אותן ונותן להן כוח להמשיך

Holocaust Remembrance Day siren sounded throughout Israel; country came to standstill; drivers halted cars on highways, pedestrians remained silent and unmoving. Main state ceremony held at Yad Vashem with PM Netanyahu, President Herzog, IDF Chief of Staff, and Holocaust survivors attending.
רס״ם אייל אוריאל ביאנקו בן 30 נהרג בדרום לבנון במהלך פעילות מבצעית
באירוע שבו נהרג ביאנקו נפצע לוחם במילואים באורח בינוני ושני לוחמים נוספים נפצעו באורח קל

IDF warns of possible increased Hezbollah rocket attacks and states 'civilians should maintain vigilance' and 'If there are changes in the situational assessment, the public will be updated accordingly'

Diaspora Ministry report: 20 Jews murdered in antisemitic incidents in the past year, including 15 in a deadly attack in Australia. Report reveals social media platforms (Meta, X, TikTok) became central engine for spreading 'fake news' and AI-based antisemitism.
שלושה לוחמי צנחנים נפצעו קשה ושבעה נוספים נפצעו בינוני וקל בהיתקלות עם חוליית מחבלים בדרום לבנון

Petah Tikva Mayor Rami Greenberg to Education Minister: high school students facing emotional and academic difficulties from war - disrupted routine, prolonged absences, psychological burden. Requested reducing external matriculation exams to core subjects only (Hebrew, Math, English, one elective), with other subjects assessed internally; reduce exam material scope; expand accommodations for fair testing conditions.

Northern residents followed negotiations in Washington with skepticism, under rocket and drone barrages. Despite PM Netanyahu's declaration that the goal is peace with Lebanon, the reality in the north appears far from it. Hezbollah barrages indicate an organization that will struggle greatly to abandon its aspirations.

Kinneret beaches opened to public following Home Front Command easing of restrictions; first visitors and vacationers arrived; soldiers from Lebanon and youth from the valley came to camp and enjoy the lake
שלושה לוחמי צה״ל נפצעו באורח קשה ולוחם נוסף נפצע באורח בינוני במסגרת היתקלות בדרום לבנון, שישה לוחמים נוספים נפצעו באורח קל

Noam Nov of Amitim for Rights: 'the mind and body don't switch off on command' and describes sharp transitions from shelters to work, children sleeping in parking lots then preparing for exams as 'not normal'
רס״ם אייל אוריאל ביאנקו בן 30 מקצרין נפל בקרב בדרום לבנון

Home Front Command announced defense policy guidelines will remain unchanged and in effect until Sunday, April 19, 2026, 20:00. Detailed restrictions by region: confrontation line - limited activity, educational activities only in protected spaces; Golan North, Upper Galilee - limited activity with protected space access during alerts; other regions - gathering limits of 5,000 people.
אביחי שטרן, ראש עיריית קריית שמונה: "אנשים נמצאים יותר מ-40 ימים מתחת לאדמה... בזמן שפה אנחנו לא צופים מתי זה יגיע אלינו"
שטרן: "אנחנו גדלנו ככה, אני הייתי מאותם ילדים שראיינו במקלטים, ולנו הבטיחו שהילדים שלנו לא יהיו במקלטים"

Jerusalem Mayor Moshe Lion announced Independence Day celebrations will proceed as planned, following consultations and noting no Home Front Command restrictions in Jerusalem preventing public gatherings.
